name: Algebraic K-theory
summary: K-groups of rings were defined and linked to topology via Quillen's higher K-theory.

name: Analysis of algorithms (Knuth)
summary: Generating functions and asymptotics are used to compute the running time of programs, creating a mathematical theory of algorithm performance.

name: Forcing: independence results enter algebra and analysis
summary: Cohen's method of forcing shows statements such as the continuum hypothesis are undecidable, and Shelah uses related techniques to show Whitehead's problem on abelian groups is independent.

name: Lojasiewicz-Simon: real-analytic gradient inequalities control geometric flows
summary: A gradient inequality from real-analytic geometry gives convergence to a unique limit for gradient-like evolution equations such as harmonic map flow and mean curvature flow.

name: Deformation theory of rings and algebras (Gerstenhaber)
summary: Kodaira-Spencer deformation ideas are carried to associative algebras, with Hochschild cohomology classifying infinitesimal deformations.

name: Computational complexity
summary: Resource-bounded computation was classified into hierarchies.

name: Rota combinatorial theory
summary: Moebius functions of posets unified inversion.

name: Computer algebra and Groebner bases
summary: Groebner bases and CAD give algorithms for polynomial systems.

name: Golod-Shafarevich: nil algebras produce infinite periodic groups
from: noncommutative ring theory (graded and nil algebras)
summary: Using a construction on nil algebras, Golod and Shafarevich built a finitely generated infinite periodic group, answering the general Burnside question negatively by algebraic means.

name: Geometric invariant theory and moduli
summary: Nineteenth-century invariant theory is recast as a quotient construction for group actions on varieties, giving moduli spaces of curves and bundles.
